subject: Architecture
title: The 15-Minute City: Everything Nearby
description: A 60-second lesson on The 15-Minute City: Everything Nearby.

hook.text: What if you could reach work, school, shops, parks, and healthcare within a 15-minute walk or bike ride?

buildup.text: Professor Carlos Moreno proposed the '15-minute city' — redesigning neighborhoods so daily needs are local.

discovery.text: Paris is leading the experiment — converting car lanes to bike paths and adding greenery to every neighborhood.

twist.text: Critics call it social control — restricting movement by design. Supporters say it's freedom from car dependency.

climax.text: Barcelona's 'superblocks' close streets to cars, creating parks and plazas — reducing pollution by 25%.

punchline.text: The best commute is none. Design the city so you never leave.

quiz.question: What is the core idea of the 15-minute city?
options: All buildings should be within 15 minutes of a highway
Daily needs are reachable within a 15-minute walk or bike ride
Public transit should arrive every 15 minutes

details.summary: The 15-minute city concept proposes that residents should reach all daily needs — work, school, healthcare, shopping, recreation — within a 15-minute walk or bike ride. Paris has championed the idea, redesigning streets and services to reduce car dependency and improve quality of life.
details.whyItMatters: The 15-minute city reimagines urban planning around human convenience rather than automotive infrastructure. It addresses commuting stress, pollution, social isolation, and neighborhood neglect with a single organizing principle.
takeaways: All daily needs within a 15-minute walk or bike ride
Paris is the leading city implementing the concept
The idea reduces car dependency and commuting stress

faq.question: Is the 15-minute city actually achievable?
faq.answer: In dense European and Asian cities, many neighborhoods already function this way. Implementation requires decentralizing services — moving offices, clinics, and schools into residential neighborhoods rather than concentrating them in distant business districts. Paris is testing this actively.

faq.question: What about people who live in suburbs?
faq.answer: The concept adapts to lower densities as a 30-minute or multi-modal model. A suburban version emphasizes local village centers accessible by bike or short drive. The principle — reducing unnecessary travel through distributed services — applies at any density, though execution differs.
